claim: Lancium holds an approved 1.2 GW grid interconnection for the Abilene Clean Campus, supplemented by behind-the-meter batteries and solar.
source: Crusoe newsroom, 'Crusoe Expands AI Data Center Campus in Abilene to 1.2 Gigawatts', 2025-03-18

claim: An initial 360 MW of on-site gas generation (GE Vernova LM2500XPRESS and Solar Titan 350 units) was completed in January 2026, with up to ~1,180 MW planned behind the meter.
source: Cleanview, 'Behind-the-meter data centers' report, Stargate Abilene profile (satellite imagery dated 2026-04-13)

claim: The campus is served by a 200 MW substation (built 2022, expanded 2024) and a larger 1 GW substation that was approaching completion in January 2026.
source: Epoch AI, AI Data Centers directory, OpenAI Stargate Abilene (satellite-based; page updated 2026-09-30)

claim: Crusoe states the Abilene site connects directly to the ERCOT grid.
source: Cleanview report quoting Crusoe statement (2026)

claim: TCEQ minor (permit-by-rule) authorisations cover 10 gas turbines and 62 diesel generators; a first major air permit application for 41 more turbines and 18 more generators was filed and is pending.
source: Floodlight News, 'This permit, common for dry cleaners, is now being used to build AI power plants', 2026-07-09

claim: Crusoe says the permitted turbines will be used only for backup power despite being permitted for continuous operation.
source: Floodlight News, 2026-07-09

claim: Cooling is direct-to-chip liquid with a zero-evaporation closed loop that is filled once and recirculated; no water-rights permit or constraint has been reported.
source: Crusoe newsroom, 2025-03-18

claim: Lancium and Crusoe executives told Abilene city leaders the loop is filled once with relatively no loss over the project life.
source: KTXS (Abilene), 'Construction on Stargate One data center campus set to run through early 2027', 2026-03-05

claim: The eighth and final building topped out in November 2025; the first two buildings (200+ MW IT) have been operational for Oracle/OpenAI since September 2025.
source: W.Media, 'Crusoe tops off final AI data center in Abilene, Texas', 2025-11-18

claim: Construction on the eight buildings is expected to run through Q1 2027, later than the mid-2026 energisation originally targeted for phase 2.
source: KTXS (Abilene), 2026-03-05

claim: Epoch estimates 421 MW of IT power operating (buildings 1-4) with buildings 5-8 projected operational by 1 November 2026 and 843 MW IT by Q4 2026.
source: Epoch AI, AI Data Centers directory (estimate; page updated 2026-09-30)

claim: A J.P. Morgan-led consortium provided a $7.1 billion construction loan to the Blue Owl/Crusoe/Primary Digital Infrastructure joint venture for phase 2 (six buildings, 1.2 GW total).
source: REBusiness Online, 'Newmark Arranges $7.1B Construction Loan for West Texas Data Center Project', 2025-05-28

claim: Total financing raised for the campus reached $11.6 billion under a $15 billion joint venture.
source: RCR Wireless, 'Crusoe secures $11.6bn for OpenAI's Stargate DC in Texas', 2025-05-22

claim: The Louisiana PSC approved a settlement (Docket U-37425) on 20 August 2025 by a 4-1 vote letting Entergy Louisiana build three combined-cycle gas plants and new transmission for the Meta campus.
source: KNOE (Monroe, LA), 'Louisiana Public Service Commission approves settlement for Meta Data Center gas plant', 2025-08-20

claim: Entergy Louisiana broke ground on the two Richland Parish Franklin Farms combined-cycle units (~1,500 MW) on 1 December 2025, with both expected operational by late 2028.
source: Entergy Louisiana newsroom, 'Entergy Louisiana breaks ground on new state-of-the-art generation facilities', 2025-12-01

claim: A second Entergy application (Docket U-37882) for seven more gas plants totalling 5,278 MW to serve the expanded 5 GW campus was fast-tracked 4-1 on 15 April 2026 and is not yet approved; the final vote is set for 18 November 2026.
source: WWNO, 'Advocates cite lack of transparency, rising costs as regulators fast-track second Meta data center', 2026-04-21

claim: Entergy's approved plan includes a 100-mile 500 kV project, the 55-acre Rayville Smalling 500/230 kV substation, two utility substations, six customer-owned substations and eight new 230 kV lines to deliver power to the Meta site; none is reported energised.
source: Industrial Info Resources, 'Louisiana Greenlights Massive Power Projects for Meta Data Center', 2025-08-27

claim: LDEQ issued the campus (as Laidley LLC) a minor-source Clean Air Act permit in July 2025 for 31 emergency diesel generators and approved an amendment on 6 June 2026 adding 44 gas boilers; the Sierra Club contends it should be a major-source permit.
source: Louisiana Illuminator, 'Meta data center pollution permit doesn't account for all its emissions, Sierra Club says', 2026-08-04

claim: Emissions from Entergy's ten gas turbines are permitted separately by the utility, not under the data centre's permit.
source: Louisiana Illuminator, 2026-08-04

claim: Meta pledges to return 100% of the facility's water consumption to local watersheds; no water withdrawal permit or source has been published.
source: Louisiana Economic Development news release, 2026-07-13

claim: Local officials voice concern about water but no constraint or permit action is documented.
source: WAFB, 'Meta's $27 billion AI data center is transforming rural Louisiana', 2026-05-12

claim: Site work moved from dirt and access roads to active construction in early 2026; the Entergy plants are due late 2028 and the data centre is not expected operational before 2028-2030.
Meta expanded the campus to nearly 10 million square feet and 5 GW of IT capacity, with 7,500 peak construction jobs.
source: Louisiana Economic Development news release, 2026-07-13

claim: Meta and Blue Owl formed a joint venture (Blue Owl 80%, Meta 20%) to fund approximately $27 billion of development costs, with Meta leasing the campus on four-year initial terms and giving a 16-year residual value guarantee.
source: Meta newsroom, 'Meta Announces Joint Venture with Funds Managed by Blue Owl Capital to Develop Hyperion Data Center', 2025-10-21

claim: Meta says it is paying $11 billion toward the ten-plant Entergy generation deal.
source: The Lens (New Orleans), 'Meta triples order of gas-fired power plants for its AI campus in Louisiana', 2026-03-30

claim: Colossus 2 (5420 Tulane Road) draws essentially all its power from behind-the-meter turbines at the former Duke Energy Southaven Power Plant site that xAI bought, estimated at ~1.3 GW across ~59 turbines, with Solaris Energy Infrastructure renting ~1,140 MW of them.
source: Cleanview, 'Behind-the-meter data centers' report, Colossus 1 & 2 profile (satellite imagery dated 2026-05-13)

claim: Colossus 1 (Paul Lowry Road) receives 150 MW of MLGW/TVA grid power with a second 150 MW requested, giving about 500 MW total with on-site generation.
source: Cleanview report, 2026

claim: MLGW states it has no new contracts at the Colossus 2 site and is not supplying power to Colossus 2; the site's general services agreement delivers about 0.5 MW.
source: Memphis Light, Gas and Water, statement on xAI at 5420 Tulane Road, 2025-07-22

claim: MDEQ issued an air permit on 10 March 2026 for 41 permanent gas turbines (about 1.2 GW) at the Southaven site; roughly 20 turbines were already running before the permit.
source: E&E News, 'xAI gets air permit for unauthorized gas turbines', 2026-03-10

claim: SELC appealed the MDEQ permit in April 2026, and under an August 2026 agreement with MDEQ the company will remove its 69 temporary mobile turbines, which SELC says can keep running until at least July 2027.
source: Memphis Flyer, 'Environmental groups call out SpacexAI and MDEQ over agreed order', 2026-08-03

claim: The $80 million Colossus Water Recycling Plant (up to 13 million gallons/day of reclaimed water), broken ground October 2025, was put on indefinite pause in April 2026, leaving the campus drawing on the Memphis Sand Aquifer.
source: Action News 5 (Memphis), 'xAI is prioritizing other projects; water plant is still planned', 2026-04-09

claim: Rep. Steve Cohen publicly urged xAI to resume the water recycling plant after its work stoppage.
source: Office of Rep. Steve Cohen, press release, 2026-04-10

claim: Epoch estimates 946 MW of IT power operating at Colossus 2 and projects 1,531 MW by Q1 2027; Musk announced 'nearly 2 gigawatts' for Colossus 1 and 2 combined.
source: Cleanview report, 2026 (construction timeline; Epoch estimate for MW per stack/campuses.csv, updated 2026-09-24)

claim: Musk said Colossus 2 had to be finished and made stable before the water plant resumes, signalling the campus is still in build-out.
source: Action News 5 quoting Elon Musk on X, 2026-04-09

claim: xAI raised a $20 billion round in October 2025 split into about $7.5 billion of equity and up to $12.5 billion of debt through an SPV that buys Nvidia GPUs for Colossus 2 and rents them to xAI for five years.
source: Free Malaysia Today (Bloomberg report), 'Nvidia to invest in Musk's xAI as part of US$20bil funding', 2025-10-08
